records.description: A real retail offer whose URL matches the registered, enabled Farfetch provider is watch-eligible.

input.title: Marc Jacobs Sac de Jour Bag

records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/watchlistCapability.ts:54-61,77-86 (WATCH_PROVIDER_REGISTRY, deriveWatchCapability) — farfetch is one of exactly two registered providers with a real re-read-by-identity adapter; isWatchableListing() (types/watchlist.ts:60-62) returns true only when watchCapability === 'refreshable_listing'.

records.description: A real retail offer from a generic Serper-sourced URL is not watch-eligible, even though it is a genuine retail offer, because its provider has no re-observation-by-identity adapter.
records.notes: supabase/functions/scan-identify/watchlistCapability.ts:42-61 — watch eligibility is gated by the provider registry (only farfetch and kickscrew), not by whether the offer is a genuine retail purchase. A real Zappos/Serper offer is still 'unsupported' because Serper has no refresh-by-identity path (watchlistCapability.ts:47-49).

records.description: A listing record that predates the watchCapability field entirely (field absent, not merely falsy) must not be treated as watchable — absence is never inferred as eligibility.

expected.reasoning: watchCapability field absent, not defaulted to refreshable_listing or unsupported

records.notes: types/watchlist.ts:60-62 — isWatchableListing() does a strict `listing?.watchCapability === 'refreshable_listing'` check; an absent field fails that strict equality and yields false, exactly like an explicit 'unsupported' value. Never inferred as watchable from absence.

records.description: A record where type is 'similar' (a similar-style web link, not a real offer) nonetheless carries watchCapability: 'refreshable_listing' by data error; the client-side eligibility check does not independently re-verify type==='retail', it trusts the server-set watchCapability field completely — this is a documented tension/gap between the two independent check functions, not an observed real-world case.

expected.computedFrom: watchCapability field only, type field not re-checked downstream

records.notes: SYNTHETIC — this exact inconsistent-data combination was never observed; it is reasoned about by composing two real, independently-verified functions: deriveWatchCapability (watchlistCapability.ts:77-86) checks type === 'retail' before ever producing 'refreshable_listing', so a real server response could never produce this combination server-side. But isWatchableListing (types/watchlist.ts:60-62) only reads watchCapability and never re-checks type, so IF a 'similar' record somehow carried watchCapability: 'refreshable_listing' (e.g. stale cache, a future bug, a malformed manual test record), the client would still compute watchable: true. This documents a tension/gap between the two independent checks, not a real production path.

records.description: A Poshmark resale offer is not watch-eligible because Poshmark, like every provider except Farfetch and KicksCrew, has no re-observation-by-identity adapter.
records.notes: no real resale provider is watch-eligible today; a 'watchable Resale' case would require a SYNTHETIC hypothetical future provider, which Section 22 permits ('watchable Resale if current contract permits') — the current contract does not permit it, so this fixture demonstrates the negative instead. Grounded in watchlistCapability.ts:47-49,54-61 (Poshmark is explicitly named as having no refresh-by-identity path, and is absent from WATCH_PROVIDER_REGISTRY).
